cards.front: Which fixative preserves stool for permanent stained smears (trichrome, iron hematoxylin), and what is 10% formalin used for?
cards.back: PVA (or SAF) preserves material for permanent stained smears. Ten percent formalin preserves eggs, cysts, and larvae for wet mounts and concentration - but formalin-fixed material cannot be permanently stained.

cards.front: Formalin-ethyl acetate concentration recovers [[1]], [[2]], and [[3]] from stool, but material fixed in formalin can never be used for trichrome staining.
cards.note: Trichrome and iron hematoxylin require PVA or SAF fixation.

cards.front: Why can morphology alone never confirm Entamoeba histolytica?
cards.back: E. histolytica and E. dispar are morphologically identical. Report the E. histolytica/dispar complex unless a species-specific antigen test or PCR resolves the identification.

cards.front: E. histolytica/dispar mature cysts have up to [[1]] nuclei with fine peripheral chromatin and splintered chromatoid bars; E. coli cysts have up to [[2]] nuclei with coarse chromatin.
cards.note: Mnemonic: 'cultured ladies eat 4-course meals' - E. coli up to 8, E. histolytica/dispar up to 4.

cards.front: What is the respective role of the thick film and the thin film in the malaria workup?
cards.back: Thick film: screens a larger blood volume for parasitemia (red cells lysed, parasites concentrated). Thin film: intact red cells allow Plasmodium species identification and staging.

cards.front: P. falciparum gametocytes are [[1]]-shaped; its rings may show [[2]] forms at the red cell margin, and several rings may infect one [[3]].
cards.note: Falciparum schizonts sequester and are rarely seen in peripheral blood.

cards.front: What are Schüffner dots, and which Plasmodium species show them?
cards.back: Fine pink-red cytoplasmic stippling seen on Giemsa-stained thin films, characteristic of P. vivax (fine) and P. ovale (coarser, sometimes called James dots). P. falciparum shows bluish Maurer's clefts instead.

cards.front: P. malariae is famous for [[1]]-shaped trophozoites and [[2]] (72-hour) fever periodicity.
cards.note: Its schizonts cluster merozoites into rosettes (6-12 merozoites).

cards.front: How are Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi distinguished on a stained blood film?
cards.back: Both are sheathed. W. bancrofti: body nuclei stop short of the tail tip (tip clear). B. malayi: two distinct subterminal nuclei in the tail. Both are sought in night blood (nocturnal periodicity).

cards.front: What is the diagnostic specimen and collection method for Enterobius vermicularis?
cards.back: A morning cellophane tape (Graham) swab of the perianal skin, taken before bathing or defecation, repeated over several mornings. Enterobius eggs are not reliably found on routine stool examination.

cards.front: Trichuris trichiura egg: barrel-shaped with [[1]] polar mucoid plugs. Hookworm egg: thin shell with a [[2]]-cell morula.
cards.note: In Philippine stools, a 'small Trichuris' with flattened plugs suggests Capillaria philippinensis.

cards.front: How are Strongyloides stercoralis rhabditiform larvae distinguished from hookworm larvae in stool?
cards.back: Strongyloides L1: long buccal cavity, small genital primordium. Hookworm L1: short buccal cavity, large genital primordium. Strongyloides passes larvae in stool - not eggs.

cards.front: How is Cryptosporidium detected in stool, and why can routine trichrome miss it?
cards.back: Modified acid-fast staining (or antigen/immunofluorescence methods) demonstrates 4-6 micrometer oocysts. The oocysts are so small that routine trichrome can overlook them.

cards.front: Giardia lamblia cysts are oval with [[1]] to [[2]] nuclei and curved [[3]] bodies; the trophozoite has two nuclei (owl face).
When should blood be collected to detect Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi microfilariae, and when for Loa loa?
cards.back: W. bancrofti and B. malayi show nocturnal periodicity: draw night blood (roughly 10 p.m. to 2 a.m.). Loa loa is diurnal: draw day blood.
cards.note: Some Pacific strains of W. bancrofti are subperiodic - follow local epidemiology.

cards.front: Knott's concentration lyses red cells with [[1]], centrifuges the sample, and examines the stained sediment for [[2]] microfilariae.
cards.note: Membrane filtration is an alternative concentration method.

cards.front: Why does a single negative blood film not exclude malaria?
cards.back: Parasitemia fluctuates as broods mature and sequester. When suspicion is high, repeat thick and thin smears at 12- to 24-hour intervals for two or three additional sets before excluding malaria.

cards.front: P. vivax infects [[1]] red cells (enlarged, distorted) with [[2]] trophozoites and fine Schüffner dots; P. ovale red cells are [[3]] with fimbriated edges.
cards.note: Ovale schizonts: up to 8 merozoites; vivax schizonts: 12-24 merozoites.
